findings.title: Upsampled function is not registered for the errors dataset
findings.body: _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True unconditionally for the errors dataset, so count() is rewritten to upsampled_count(), but the upsampled_count SnQLFunction added in this PR is only registered in src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py. The errors dataset uses its own function converter, so an allowlisted query explicitly using dataset=errors will fail query validation/building with an unknown-function error instead of returning upsampled counts.

findings.title: Eligibility check uses the outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is passed the closure variable dataset rather than the scoped_dataset argument to _get_event_stats. The dashboard-widget split path calls _get_event_stats with split_dataset=discover or the original scoped dataset, so the decision is made for the wrong dataset: error split queries originating from metrics/discover datasets will not be upsampled, and conversely a transformation can be decided based on a dataset that is not actually executed.

findings.title: Discover error detection inspects request.GET instead of the executed query and matches negations
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query only looks at request.GET['query'] and does a substring check for 'event.type:error'. It ignores the query argument actually passed to _get_event_stats, including internally constructed dashboard-split queries such as '(...) AND !event.type:transaction', so legitimate error queries can be missed. The substring check also returns True for '!event.type:error' and for mixed queries such as 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction', applying sum(sample_weight) to non-error/transaction rows where upsampling must not apply.

findings.title: upsampled_count sums sample_weight without handling missing weights
findings.body: The aggregate is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no coalesce/ifNull fallback to 1. Events in allowlisted projects that predate client error sampling, were not client-sampled, or otherwise have a NULL/absent sample_weight contribute NULL rather than counting as one event; if all rows in a bucket are NULL the sum is NULL and toInt64(NULL) can error or produce no count. This silently undercounts (or breaks) ordinary count() queries after the rewrite, contrary to a plain count() for unsampled events.

findings.title: Cache key uses Python hash() of project IDs and is collision-prone
findings.body: The eligibility cache key is built with hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). hash() is not a stable, collision-resistant identifier for a set of projects: different project sets can collide and share a cached eligibility result, causing upsampling to be applied to non-allowlisted projects or withheld from allowlisted ones for 60 seconds. A deterministic key such as the comma-joined sorted IDs should be used instead. invalidate_upsampling_cache repeats the same flawed key and is also never called when the allowlist option changes.

findings.title: Stray sentry-repo subproject file committed
findings.body: This added file contains only 'Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a', i.e. an accidentally committed nested-repository/gitlink artifact pointing at the base commit. It is unrelated to error upsampling and will create a broken/unexpected submodule entry in the repository if merged.

findings.title: Falsy client_sample_rate is dropped and existing sample_rate is overwritten
findings.body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling guards with 'if client_sample_rate:', so a present value of 0/0.0 is silently ignored, and for any truthy value it unconditionally overwrites normalized_data['sample_rate'] even if a legitimate sample_rate was already supplied by the SDK/event. In tests this can mask the intended sampling metadata and produce events whose stored sample_weight does not reflect the fixture the author specified.
